dimensions.label: Regulatory quality
dimensions.definition: Perceptions of the government's ability to design and implement policies and regulations that promote private sector development.

dimensions.label: Rule of law
dimensions.definition: Perceptions of the extent to which agents respect and follow the rules of society, including contract enforcement, property rights, the police, courts, and the likelihood of crime and violence.

dimensions.label: Government effectiveness
dimensions.definition: Perceptions of the quality of public services, the civil service, policy formulation and implementation, and the credibility of a government's commitment to such policies.

dimensions.label: Control of corruption
dimensions.definition: Perceptions of the extent to which public power is used for private gain, including both petty and grand corruption, as well as capture of the state by elites and private interests.

dimensions.label: Voice and accountability
dimensions.definition: Perceptions of the extent to which citizens can participate in selecting their government, and of accountability mechanisms such as access to information, oversight bodies and the media.

dimensions.label: Political stability
dimensions.definition: Perceptions of the likelihood of political instability and of challenges to or changes in political authority through violent, coercive, or unconstitutional means.

milestones.title: Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2026 (No. 8 of 2026)
milestones.detail: Presidential assent on 7 April 2026, published in the Gazette of India on 8 April. Comes into force on dates the Centre notifies, which may differ for each Act in the Schedule: watch for commencement notifications.
milestones.source: Gazette of India (Extraordinary) Part II Section 1

milestones.title: Jan Vishwas Bill 2026 introduced
milestones.detail: Introduced in Lok Sabha to amend 80 central Acts, decriminalising or rationalising offences and penalties. Passed by Lok Sabha on 1 April and Rajya Sabha on 2 April 2026.

milestones.title: Jan Vishwas Bill 2025 withdrawn
milestones.detail: Withdrawn to make way for a wider Bill reflecting the Select Committee's recommendations.

milestones.title: Select Committee reports on Jan Vishwas Bill 2025
milestones.detail: Recommended further changes to the 17 Acts and amendments to 65 other Acts.

milestones.title: Jan Vishwas Bill 2025 introduced
milestones.detail: Sought to amend 17 central Acts; referred to a Select Committee of Lok Sabha (Chair: Tejasvi Surya).

milestones.title: Jan Vishwas Bill 2022 passed by Parliament
milestones.detail: Passed by Lok Sabha on 27 July 2023 and Rajya Sabha on 2 August 2023. 42 central Acts amended.

milestones.title: Joint Parliamentary Committee reports on Jan Vishwas Bill 2022
milestones.detail: Committee report presented before the Bill was taken up for passing.

milestones.title: Jan Vishwas Bill 2022 introduced
milestones.detail: Introduced in Lok Sabha and referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee the same day. Amends 42 laws, converting several fines into penalties that do not need court prosecution and removing imprisonment for many offences.
